edges.description: Pld4-deficient mice reproduce autoimmunity with cell-intrinsic expansion of plasmacytoid dendritic cells and plasma cells, elevated anti-dsDNA/anti-dsRNA autoantibodies, splenomegaly and glomerular immune-complex nephritis, closely mirroring the human phenotype.
edges.limitations: TLR9 plays context-dependent, strain-specific roles in PLD3/PLD4-deficient mice (cooperating with TLR7/cGAS-STING on the C57BL/6 background used here, but acting differently on a BALB/c background), so the precise balance of TLR7 versus TLR9 contribution observed in this model may not generalize across genetic backgrounds or directly to all human patients.
edges.target: Autoantibody Production and Plasma Cell Expansion

edges.description: Eight weeks of oral baricitinib substantially reduced autoantibody titres, spleen size, renal inflammatory gene expression and glomerular IgG/C3 deposition in Pld4-/- mice, rescuing the type I interferon-driven phenotype and nominating JAK inhibition as a mechanism-targeted therapy.

nodes.description: Pld4-deficient mice show cell-intrinsic expansion of plasmacytoid dendritic cells and plasma cells and significantly elevated anti-double-stranded-DNA (dsDNA) and anti-dsRNA autoantibodies and total IgG, establishing a self-reactive humoral response downstream of the dendritic-cell interferon signature.

nodes.description: Autoantibody-nucleic-acid immune complexes deposit in the glomerulus, producing proliferative or membranoproliferative lupus nephritis in every reported patient. Pld4-deficient mice reproduce glomerular basement membrane thickening and IgG/C3 deposition, with renal inflammatory genes (Tnf, Cxcl10, Mx2, Ifng) most prominently elevated in the kidney.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in PLD4 lead to systemic lupus erythematosus.
evidence.snippet: All of the patients presented with a renal phenotype. Kidney biopsy showed proliferative lupus nephritis

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in PLD4 lead to systemic lupus erythematosus.
evidence.snippet: Pld4−/− mice displayed severe nephritic phenotypes, including thickening of the glomerular basement membrane

nodes.description: PLD4 normally localizes to endolysosomes and degrades single-stranded RNA and DNA there. With exonuclease activity lost, ssDNA and ssRNA substrates accumulate uncleaved in this compartment instead of being cleared.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in PLD4 lead to systemic lupus erythematosus.
evidence.snippet: the ssDNA in all mutant-PLD4 groups remained uncleaved

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in PLD4 lead to systemic lupus erythematosus.
evidence.snippet: PLD4 15–18 is highly expressed in DCs, monocytes and B cells. It is a 5′ exonuclease that localizes in the endolysosomes and can cleave single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) and single-stranded DNA (ssDNA)

nodes.description: Janus kinase inhibition with baricitinib suppressed the elevated type I interferon pathway in patient PBMCs ex vivo and, in Pld4-deficient mice, improved body-weight gain, lowered anti-dsDNA/anti-dsRNA autoantibody titres and spleen size, and reduced renal inflammatory gene expression and glomerular immune-complex deposition. It has not yet been used to treat a patient clinically; the evidence is ex vivo (patient PBMCs) and in a mouse model.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in PLD4 lead to systemic lupus erythematosus.
evidence.snippet: the baricitinib-treated mice showed significant improvements in body-weight gain, plasma levels of anti-dsDNA and anti-dsRNA antibodies, and spleen size compared with the untreated mice

nodes.description: All five reported patients developed proliferative or membranoproliferative lupus nephritis on kidney biopsy, in two cases progressing to maintenance haemodialysis.

Purified mutant protein and patient-derived endogenous PLD4 both show markedly impaired single-stranded nucleic acid exonuclease activity relative to wild type.

nodes.description: STING is phosphorylated and activated in PLD4-deficient cells. STING inhibitors (H-151, C-176) and PLD4/STING1 double knockout both attenuate the type I interferon response, establishing a cGAS-STING-dependent amplification step downstream of TLR7/9 hyperactivation, consistent with prior PLD3/PLD4-deficient mouse models.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in PLD4 lead to systemic lupus erythematosus.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in PLD4 lead to systemic lupus erythematosus.
evidence.snippet: PLD4 and STING1 double-KO cell lines corroborated these findings. Both qPCR and western blot analysis demonstrated the rescue of type I IFN pathway activation after STING ablation, whereas NF-κB signalling showed only partial restoration

nodes.description: Accumulated endolysosomal ssRNA and ssDNA excessively engage the nucleic-acid sensors TLR7 and TLR9. Both full-length and activated TLR7 are upregulated in patient PBMCs, with concomitant elevation of TLR9 and the downstream adaptors TRAF6, IRAK1 and IRAK4, most prominently in dendritic cells and monocytes.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in PLD4 lead to systemic lupus erythematosus.
evidence.snippet: PLD4 loss-of-function mutations led to excessive activation of Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) and TLR9

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in PLD4 lead to systemic lupus erythematosus.
evidence.snippet: Genes encoding TLR7/9 and TLR signalling pathway-related molecules, including TLR7, TLR9, TRAF6, IRAK1 and IRAK4, were also significantly elevated in DCs of patients P1 and P2 compared with in the healthy controls

nodes.description: Type I interferon pathway genes are significantly upregulated in patient PBMCs at baseline and after TLR9-agonist stimulation, with the signal concentrated in PLD4-expressing dendritic cells and monocytes. NF-kB and MAPK signaling are also activated. This gene-expression and signaling phenotype is rescued by JAK inhibition.
